The law provides detailed regulations regarding the management of fishery ports, specifically defining the duties and authority of the Syahbandar (harbor master) at these locations. It also establishes formal legal provisions for fishery levies in Indonesia and defines the specific duties of fishery supervisors, ensuring a structured regulatory environment for the country's maritime economy.

Furthermore, UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 encompasses trade regulations and establishes the necessary requirements for business and investment licenses within the sector.

The law provides detailed regulations regarding the management of fishery ports, specifically defining the duties and authority of the Syahbandar (harbor master) at these locations. It also establishes formal legal provisions for fishery levies in Indonesia and defines the specific duties of fishery supervisors. To ensure regulatory enforcement, the law establishes a fishery court and defines the authority and powers of the investigator within the fisheries sector.

Enacted in 2009, this law establishes the general provisions and principles for the management and utilization of Indonesia's fish resources. Its core purpose is to ensure the sustainability of aquatic resources while providing protections for both maritime and inland water systems.

This legislation acts as an amendment to Undang-Undang Nomor 31 Tahun 2004, providing a comprehensive framework for fishery business operations, including the handling, processing, and quality standards of fish, notably those outlined in Article 25A. It covers a broad spectrum of activities such as fishing operations, aquaculture, and fish farming. Furthermore, UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 encompasses trade regulations and establishes the necessary requirements for business and investment licenses within the fisheries sector.

Additionally, UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 governs the logistical and administrative aspects of the maritime industry, including the registration of fishing vessels, the issuance of sailing permits, and the management of fishery ports. The law specifically defines the duties and authority of the Syahbandar (harbor master) at these locations and establishes formal legal provisions for fishery levies and the specific duties of fishery supervisors. 

To ensure regulatory enforcement, the law provides a framework for criminal procedures and judicial processes within the fisheries sector. This includes the establishment of a fishery court and specific court sub-units, as well as defining the authority and powers of investigators tasked with handling fishery-related crimes and judicial procedures.

The law specifically defines the duties and authority of the Syahbandar (harbor master) at these locations and establishes formal legal provisions for fishery levies and the specific duties of fishery supervisors. 

To ensure regulatory enforcement, the law provides a framework for criminal procedures and judicial processes within the fisheries sector. UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 is a legislative law and formal legal regulation issued by the Republic of Indonesia that serves as the primary legal framework for the nation’s aquatic and fisheries sectors. Enacted in 2009, this act establishes the general provisions and principles for the management and utilization of Indonesia's fish resources. Its core purpose is to ensure the sustainability of aquatic resources while providing comprehensive protections for both maritime and inland water systems. As a regulatory document, it provides official explanations for specific articles and became effective on the date of its promulgation.

This legislation acts as an amendment to Undang-Undang Nomor 31 Tahun 2004, providing a comprehensive framework for fishery business operations. The scope of the law covers a broad spectrum of activities, including fishing operations, aquaculture, and fish farming. It contains specific provisions regarding the handling, processing, and quality standards of fish, notably those outlined in Article 25A, and includes various specific legal articles such as Pasal 100D. Furthermore, UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 encompasses trade regulations and establishes the necessary requirements for business and investment licenses within the fisheries sector.

Additionally, UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 governs the logistical and administrative aspects of the maritime industry, including the registration of fishing vessels, the issuance of sailing permits, and the management of fishery ports. The law specifically defines the duties and authority of the Syahbandar (harbor master) at these locations and establishes formal legal provisions for fishery levies and the specific duties of fishery supervisors. To ensure regulatory enforcement, the law provides a framework for criminal procedures, judicial processes, and legal penalties within the fisheries sector. This includes the establishment of a fishery court and specific court sub-units, as well as defining the authority and powers of investigators tasked with handling fishery-related crimes and judicial procedures.

Its core purpose is to ensure the sustainability of aquatic resources while providing comprehensive protections for both maritime and inland water systems. As a regulatory document, it provides official explanations for specific articles and became effective on the date of its promulgation.

This legislation acts as an amendment to Undang-Undang Nomor 31 Tahun 2004, providing a comprehensive framework for fishery business operations, including fishing operations, aquaculture, and fish farming. The scope of the law covers a broad spectrum of activities, including trade regulations and the establishment of requirements for business and investment licenses within the fisheries sector. Furthermore, it contains specific provisions regarding the handling, processing, and quality standards of fish, notably those outlined in Article 25A, and includes various specific legal articles such as Pasal 100D.

Additionally, UU Nomor 45 Tahun 2009 governs the logistical and administrative aspects of the maritime industry, including the registration of fishing vessels, the issuance of sailing permits, and the management of fishery ports. The law specifically defines the duties and authority of the Syahbandar (harbor master) at these locations and establishes formal legal provisions for fishery levies and the specific duties of fishery supervisors. To ensure regulatory enforcement, the law provides a framework for criminal procedures, judicial processes, and legal penalties within the fisheries sector. This includes the establishment of a fishery court and specific court sub-units, as well as defining the authority and powers of investigators tasked with handling fishery-related crimes and judicial procedures.
